Avodah Zarah 7a:8.english: The Sages taught: A person may not say to another on Shabbat: Does it seem that you will join me this evening? This is prohibited, as the speaker is hinting that he would like to hire the person being spoken to for labor after the conclusion of Shabbat. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says: A person may say to another on Shabbat: Does it seem that you will join me this evening? In this case, he is not asking the person explicitly. Rabba bar bar Ḥana says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa.

Avodah Zarah 7b:3.english: GEMARA: Rav Taḥlifa bar Avdimi says that Shmuel says: With regard to Christians, according to the statement of Rabbi Yishmael, it is always prohibited to engage in business with them. Since their festival, Sunday, occurs every week, and the three days before and after it are prohibited, one cannot engage in business with them on any day of the week.

Avodah Zarah 7b:4.english: The mishna teaches: And the Rabbis say: It is prohibited to engage in business with gentiles before their festivals, but it is permitted to do so after their festivals. The Gemara asks: The statement of these Rabbis is identical to that of the first tanna in the mishna on 2a! The Gemara answers: The question of whether the three days include the days of the festivals themselves or whether they refer to the three days without the festivals is the difference between them. The first tanna holds that the prohibition applies to the three days without the festivals, and the Rabbis in this mishna hold that it applies to the days of the festivals themselves and the days preceding them, totaling three days.

Avodah Zarah 7b:5.english: If you wish, say instead that the status of profits earned from engaging in business with a gentile is the difference between them. The first tanna holds that if one violated the prohibition and engaged in business with a gentile, the profit is permitted, and the Rabbis in this mishna hold that if one engaged in business with a gentile, the profit is prohibited.

Avodah Zarah 7b:6.english: And if you wish, say instead that the ruling of Shmuel is the difference between them. As Shmuel says: In the Diaspora, it is prohibited to engage in business with gentiles only on the day of their festival itself. The first tanna accepts the statement of Shmuel, but the Rabbis in this mishna do not accept the statement of Shmuel.

Avodah Zarah 7b:7.english: And if you wish, say instead that the ruling of Naḥum the Mede is the difference between them. As it is taught in a baraita that Naḥum the Mede says: It is prohibited to engage in business with gentiles only one day before their festival. The first tanna does not accept the statement of Naḥum the Mede, but the Rabbis in this mishna accept the statement of Naḥum the Mede.

Avodah Zarah 7b:8.english: The Gemara returns to discuss the matter itself. Naḥum the Mede says: It is prohibited to engage in business with gentiles only one day before their festival. The other Sages said to him: This matter should be lost and not stated, as it is not the halakha. The Gemara asks: But aren’t there the Rabbis in this mishna, who hold in accordance with his opinion? The Gemara answers: Who are the Rabbis mentioned there? It is Naḥum the Mede himself.

Consigli alimentari contro la ritenzione idrica

Innanzitutto occorre ridurre il consumo di sale, che è il principale responsabile del ristagno di liquidi. Non bisogna però solo limitare l’aggiunta del sale alle pietanze, ma anche evitare tutti quei cibi che contengono sale nascosto (insaccati, formaggi stagionati, snack salati, cibi in scatola). È fondamentale, inoltre, bere molta acqua per aiutare i reni ad espellere i liquidi ed eliminare le tossine. Importante è anche assumere il giusto quantitativo di fibre per garantire la regolarità intestinale, la cui mancanza favorisce l'insorgenza della ritenzione idrica. Spazio, quindi, a cereali integrali, legumi, frutta e verdura, preferendo alimenti freschi e di stagione. In particolare, alcuni cibi hanno proprietà drenanti e depurative: tra questi troviamo l'ananas (che favorisce la digestione e aiuta a combattere l'infiammazione), il cetriolo (composto per il 96% di acqua), le cipolle (dal potere diuretico), il sedano e il finocchio (perfetti anche come spuntino sgonfia-pancia), il kiwi (ricco di potassio e vitamina C), i frutti rossi (che migliorano il microcircolo). Anche alcune bevande possono essere molto utili: tra queste, le tisane a base di betulla, equiseto e tarassaco, ma anche il tè verde, noto per le sue proprietà drenanti e antiossidanti. Accanto a un’alimentazione corretta, è fondamentale praticare regolare attività fisica, come camminate a passo svelto, nuoto e bicicletta. Vediamo insieme una proposta di menù settimanale contro la ritenzione idrica.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:3:1.hebrew: לעולם אסור - שלשה לפניו ושלשה לאחריו והוא עצמו, כלומר: כל שבעת ימי השבת:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:3:1.english: It is always prohibited: [This means] three days before Sunday and three days after it, as well as the day itself; that is to say, all seven days of the week.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:4:1.hebrew: תנא קמא סבר הן בלא אידיהן - כדדייקינן לעיל: דקתני "לפני אידיהן של עובדי כוכבים שלשה ימים", שמע מינה: שלשה לפניהם לבד האיד קאמר:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:4:1.english: The first tanna holds [it means] the days without the festival: As we inferred above from the fact that the first mishna teaches: 'Before the festivals of gentiles three days'. Conclude from it that he meant three days before them, besides the festival.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:4:2.hebrew: ורבנן בתראי - דלא יהבו סימנא, איכא למימר: הואיל ולא אשכחן מידי ביניהן, איכא למימר בהא אתו לאפלוגי: דהן ואידיהן שלשה קאמר:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:4:2.english: And the later Rabbis: Since they did not give an indicator, it can be said that since we do not find anything else between the two mishnayot, they must come to disagree about this: That the festival and the preceding days together are three.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:5:1.hebrew: רבנן בתראי סברי נשא ונתן אסור - סתמא קאמרינן, ולא קתני "אסור לשאת ולתת" כתנא קמא, דמשמע: לכתחלה הוא דלא, הא דיעבד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:5:1.english: The later Rabbis hold [if] one engaged in business it is prohibited: They state the law plainly, and it does not teach 'it is prohibited to engage in business' as the first tanna did, which would imply that the prohibition is only ab initio but that after the fact it is permitted.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:6:1.hebrew: בגולה - אין העובדי כוכבים אדוקין כל כך בעבודת כוכבים, כדאמרינן לקמן: "עובדי כוכבים שבחוצה לארץ לאו עובדי עבודת כוכבים נינהו וכולי". ועוד: דמסתפינן מינייהו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:6:1.english: In the Diaspora: The gentiles are not so devoted to idol worship, as we say later: 'Gentiles outside the Land of Israel are not [truly] idol worshippers, etc.' Moreover, we are afraid of them.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:6:2.hebrew: רבנן בתראי לית להו דשמואל - דכיון דלא מסיים בהדיא במאי פליגי, איכא למימר: לטפויי אתו, דשמעינן לתנא קמא דקאמר: "לפני אידיהן אסור לשאת ולתת עמהם", וסתמא דמילתא - כשאין יד עובדי כוכבים תקיפה על ישראל קא אמר; ואתו אינהו למימר: לפני אידיהן לעולם אסורין. ואיפכא ליכא לשנויי, דתתריץ שפיר: דסתם תנא בתרא לטפויי אתא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:6:2.english: The later Rabbis do not hold like Shmuel: Since it is not explicitly stated in what way they disagree, one can say they came to add a stringency. We heard the first tanna say: 'before their festivals it is prohibited to engage in business with them', and the plain meaning is that he spoke only when the gentiles do not have the upper hand over Israel. These [later Rabbis] then came to say: 'before their festivals it is always prohibited'. The opposite cannot be suggested, as the explanation is settled well only if a later unattributed tanna is assumed to come to add a stringency.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:7:1.hebrew: רבנן בתראי אית להו כנחום - דלא יהבי חושבנא, אלא "אסור" סתמא קאמרי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:7:1.english: The later Rabbis hold like Naḥum: Since they did not specify a count of days, but rather said 'prohibited' in a general sense.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:8:1.hebrew: נשתקע הדבר - לא יצא דבר זה מפי אדם לעולם. לשון אחר: לא יצא דבר זה לחוץ:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 7b:8:1.english: The matter should be lost: This statement should never have been uttered by anyone. Another explanation: This matter should not have been publicized.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 7b.english: The Jerusalem Talmud records a dispute regarding the reasoning of Rabbi Yishmael. Some explain that his ruling is based on the fact that gentiles are accustomed to adding days to their festival, similar to the Jewish custom of observing the day after a Festival as Isru Ĥag; therefore, the days following their festival are considered like the festival day itself. Rabbi Abba explains that the reasoning is that if a gentile knows that a Jew will not conduct business with him on the day following the festival, he will diminish his celebration of idol worship in order to save resources for the next day. The early commentaries explained the ruling according to the reasoning that the gentile “goes and gives thanks,” meaning that because of the proximity to the day of his idol’s festival, he goes and gives thanks on the following days as well. Alternatively, the prohibition against conducting business during the three days after the festival is a rabbinic decree due to the prohibition that applies during the three days before the festival (see Ra’ah and Meiri).

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 7b:2.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yishmael says: Three days before them, meaning before the festivals of the gentiles, and three days after them, it is prohibited to engage in business with the gentiles. And the Rabbis say: Before their festivals it is prohibited, but after their festivals it is permitted.
